dod_intent_evidence: Genuine and extensive: 2020 U.S. Navy magnetometer contract for Naval Undersea Warfare Center, A-FORT SBIR (Army xTechSearch 7 winner, GPS-denied soldier tracking), and a Jan 2026 AFWERX Phase II SBIR for a pilot locator beacon (News section) — but this sits on top of a 30-year track record of already-fielded defense sensor products.
what_they_do: Magnetic/inertial sensor and sensor-fusion module manufacturer (RM3100, FORT/A-FORT) for GPS-denied positioning, sold as OEM components into defense and commercial platforms.
notes: The company's own 'Products at Work' page names already-fielded defense integrations across nine different platforms (NUWC towed arrays, Liquid Robotics Wave Glider, Atlas SeaFox mine-disposal ROV, QinetiQ Talon bomb-disposal robot, L3 Warrior Systems STORM, Senop target-acquisition system, PackBot, Sparton sonobuoys, FLIR surveillance) built over 30 years. That is a mature, proven, revenue-generating defense OEM sensor supplier, not a $5-10M company at risk from one dead transition — new efforts like A-FORT and the AFWERX pilot beacon are incremental product-line extensions for an established business, not existential prototype-to-fielded bets.
